items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"The Constitution is a means of bringing about peaceful democratic transformation. The Constitution limits power so that no group can dominate others. The Preamble promises equality of status and of opportunity. The Constitution embodies a moral vision of liberty, equality, fraternity and justice."
(i) Explain the term 'philosophy of the Constitution', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: The Constituent Assembly debates are important. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "The Constitution is only a legal document without any values." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) The moral values and ideals, such as liberty, equality and justice, that underlie the Constitution. (ii) They reveal the reasons and values behind the provisions of the Constitution. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It embodies a moral vision of liberty, equality, fraternity and justice.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) The moral values and ideals, such as liberty, equality and justice, that underlie the Constitution. (ii) They reveal the reasons and values behind the provisions of the Constitution. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It embodies a moral vision of liberty, equality, fraternity and justice.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the political philosophy of the Indian Constitution is correct?
items.answer: Indian secularism does not mean a wall of separation between religion and the state.
items.markingKey: (b) The others are wrong: It follows principled distance and allows intervention for freedom and equality. It also recognises the rights of religious and linguistic minorities. It was granted from the start in 1950.
options: The Constitution recognises only individual rights and no community rights.
Indian secularism does not mean a wall of separation between religion and the state.
Indian secularism requires complete separation between religion and the state.
Universal adult franchise was introduced in India only in the 1970s.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on procedural achievements and criticisms of the Constitution and answer the questions that follow.
"The Constituent Assembly reached decisions through deliberation and a spirit of accommodation. Critics say the Constitution is unrepresentative because the Constituent Assembly was not elected by universal franchise. Critics say the Constitution is alien because it borrows from Western constitutions."
(i) The criticism that the Constitution borrows heavily from Western constitutions is that it is: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'unwieldy' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The Constitution is called a product of deliberation. (2)
items.answer: (i) alien (ii) A criticism that the Constitution is too long and detailed. (iii) The Constituent Assembly discussed every provision carefully and sought consensus.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) alien (ii) A criticism that the Constitution is too long and detailed. (iii) The Constituent Assembly discussed every provision carefully and sought consensus.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about procedural achievements and criticisms of the Constitution is correct?
